Subject: Decision criteria: latency/cost/SLA follow-up (Finova)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Key decision criteria you called out: latency (P95 target), unit cost (tokens/embedding), deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and SLA guarantees for production.
- From the call: target P95 inference latency ~150ms for short prompt paths (average sequence ~128 tokens), and cost sensitivity for high-volume inference (targeting a ~30% reduction vs current vendor).
- Deployment: you indicated preference for Dedicated in-cloud for initial rollout, with Private (VPC) as a requirement for any regulated data later in the roadmap.
- Procurement/legal asks: Priya (CFO) will drive procurement; Chris (Head of Security) will own the security questionnaire and data residency requirements.

Attached: Redwood-SLA-draft.pdf (draft SLA for review) and a decision criteria spreadsheet to capture any updates. Can you confirm: 1) final economic buyer(s), 2) expected procurement timeline, and 3) whether the 150ms P95 target is end-to-end (app -> inference) or just model-server latency?

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm stakeholders and timeline
2) Technical sync with Rishi to discuss throughput and sequence-length assumptions (I can set up for next week)
3) Provide any security/compliance artifacts Chris needs (we have SOC 2 + audit report ready)

If this looks right, I’ll circulate an action tracker and proposed dates.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0187

Subject: Re: Decision criteria: latency/cost/SLA follow-up (Finova)

Marissa —

Appreciate the summary, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Stakeholders:
  - Economic buyer / procurement owner: Priya Singh (CFO) — she will own contract & budget approvals.
  - Security / compliance: Chris Lopez (Head of Security) — will coordinate the questionnaire and any data-residency requirements.
  - Product/engineering: me (Alex) and Lina (not on thread) for performance sign-off.

- Latency: the 150ms P95 target is for end-to-end user-facing responses for short prompts (sub-200 tokens). There’s some leeway for longer chains, but that P95 needs to hold for the primary search/assist flows.

- Cost: our target is approximately 25–35% reduction in per-inference unit cost versus current supplier; we’ll track cost per 1k requests as a proxy.

- Deployment: we’d like to start on Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool in us-east) and evaluate Private later if legal requires it for specific data sets.

- Procurement timeline: Priya expects a 3–5 week procurement window once we have a final SLA and contract redlines. Legal will look at the SLA in week 1.

I’ve attached our completed decision-criteria sheet (finova-decision-criteria.xlsx) with the latency/cost numbers and a short note from Chris on security items.

Next step: yes to a technical sync. Can we do Rishi + Marcus + Alex + Chris next Wed (2028-03-28) at 10am ET?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Harper
Head of Product — Search & Assist
alex.harper@finova.com

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and for filling the sheet. A couple of quick clarifications so Rishi & Marcus can size the technical ask correctly: 

1) When you say 150ms P95 end-to-end, can you confirm typical client-side pre/post processing time? If there’s ~50ms on the client side our model-server target should be ~100ms P95.
2) Typical request shape: you mentioned ~128 tokens average; what is peak concurrency we should assume (concurrent requests per second) and batchability?
3) Data residency: Chris, can you confirm whether the requirement is strict US-only region or specific regions (us-east vs us-west)?

On the SLA: our draft covers 99.9% uptime and standard crediting for downtime; if Priya/legal need tighter terms we can escalate to our contracts team, but it may require a reserved capacity commitment.

I’ll schedule the technical sync for 2028-03-28 10:00am ET as suggested — Rishi will cover throughput and batching profiles, Marcus will cover quantization/instance-sizing, and I’ll cover procurement/contract next steps.

Action items I’ll take: circulate calendar invite, drop a short pre-read (latency profiles + suggested instance types), and link to the SLA draft for Priya/legal review.

Best,
